newsitem.title: USA: RR Donnelley to sell Stream, but has no firm deals.
newsitem.headline: RR Donnelley to sell Stream, but has no firm deals.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co, the world's largest commercial printing firm, on Monday confirmed it plans to sell its majority owned Stream International division, although there are no firm commitments so far.

"We do not have a definitive approach, a transaction or a timeline (for a Stream sale)," William Lowe, a Donnelley spokesman, told Reuters. "All I can say is we're looking at all kinds of options, including the sale of all or part of the business."

Stream operates three divisions related to the computer software industry. One unit manages call-in help desks for such companies as Microsoft Corp, another translates software into foreign languages and the third sells, installs and manages software for large corporations. Stream posted 1995 revenues of $1.5 billion.
According to a report in the December 16 Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed sources familiar with the plan, Donnelley is assessing ways to sell the operation piecemeal.
"(A sale of Stream) would be a positive event in the near term in that it will eliminate operating expenses and reduce interest expense," James Dougherty, an analyst for Dean Witter Reynolds, said.

"But on the other side of the coin," he continued, "it's yet another business aimed to expand Donnelley beyond the traditional printing operation that just didn't work. You now get back to being just a printing company, and that doesn't lead to great multiples."

Analysts said Stream may have lost as much as $75 million in the last two years, according to the Wall Street Journal report. The company declined to confirm that figure, but said it had planned to exit the business almost from the time it formed the company in 1995 as part of a venture with Bain Capital Inc and Stream's management team.
"We've been saying we planned to sell our 80-percent stake in Stream for quite a while," Donnelley's Lowe said. "We've had a long-stated exit policy."
Setting a price for Stream's parts is not expected to be an easy task, said Rudolph Hokanson, an analyst for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
